messages.content:
You are GoodIdea, turning one decision the user already made into an MVP boundary.
The decision below is settled. Build on it. Never re-ask it, never propose the other path, and never widen the product beyond what this first version needs.
The first version must be buildable with no real money, no live account, no credentials for a third-party service, and no external side effects.
excluded names what this version deliberately does not do, and must include the outcome the user hoped for when nothing can promise it. Nothing may appear in both included and excluded.
acceptance_criteria are checks someone can run against the built thing and get a yes or no. Not intentions, not qualities.
user_flow steps are short labels a person scans, not sentences: name the action and stop. included, excluded and assumptions are each one short phrase for the same reason. Detail belongs in the acceptance criteria, where it is checked.
implementation_order is the order a coding agent should build in, starting with what makes the rest testable.
approval_prompt asks the user to confirm this exact boundary. approval_why says what approving freezes. Neither may claim the product will succeed.
what_we_know_about_the_user is what this person told us in this or an earlier session. Fit the first version to it: do not propose work they said they cannot do, and do not propose a direction they already rejected. It is what they said about themselves, not evidence, so never cite it as a finding.
Write every human-readable field in English.
Reply with exactly one JSON object and nothing else. It must satisfy this JSON Schema:
{"description": "A feasibility path and MVP boundary written by a model for one decided path.\n\nGenerating this does not approve it. {
  "idea": "Build me a product that trades stocks automatically and makes money.",
  "decision_the_user_made": "I already trade a moving-average crossover rule by hand.",
  "decided_path": "existing_rules",
  "core_uncertainty": "Whether any specific algorithmic strategy can reliably produce net positive returns after accounting for transaction costs, slippage, taxes, and changing market regimes.",
  "outcome_the_user_hopes_for": "Consistent financial returns from automated stock market participation.",
  "market_reality": "Authoritative guidance establishes that every investment involves risk and high guaranteed returns do not exist, while brokerages like Alpaca and Interactive Brokers provide APIs and paper trading environments specifically for testing automated code without financial exposure.",
  "honest_boundary": "No source confirms that any specific algorithmic strategy can reliably produce net positive returns after costs, nor can any tool guarantee that an automated product will make money.",
  "safe_validation_step": "Connect to a paper trading environment via a brokerage API to verify your code executes logic correctly in a real-time simulation without risking funds.",
  "established_facts": [
    "Every investment involves risk and high guaranteed investment returns do not exist.",
    "Alpaca provides a real-time simulation environment for testing trading code without routing orders to a live exchange.",
    "Interactive Brokers offers an API for automated trading and a paper account for testing strategies without risking capital."
  ]
}

acceptance_criteria: System generates buy signal when fast MA crosses above slow MA on configured ticker
System generates sell signal when fast MA crosses below slow MA on configured ticker
All generated signals result in corresponding paper trade orders via API
Trade log records timestamp, signal type, price, and quantity for each action
System operates continuously for at least one full market session without crashing
No live account endpoints are called during execution
payload.approval_prompt: Confirm this MVP boundary: a paper-trading-only executor for your moving average crossover rule that validates code correctness without risking capital or promising returns.
payload.approval_why: Approving freezes the scope to risk-free logic validation only; it does not imply the strategy will be profitable or suitable for live trading.
assumptions: User has valid paper trading API credentials
User’s crossover rule is fully defined with specific MA periods
Local machine can maintain persistent connection during market hours
Paper API provides sufficient historical data for signal calculation
constraints: Must use paper trading API only
No real money or live accounts
No paid data feeds or services
payload.feasibility_summary: Buildable using free brokerage paper trading APIs and open-source libraries to automate the user's existing moving average crossover logic in a risk-free simulation environment.
implementation_order: Implement MA crossover signal generator with configurable periods
Integrate paper trading API client with authentication
Connect signal generator to order execution function
Add trade logging to local CSV file
Create configuration loader for ticker and MA parameters
Build main loop with session duration control
included: Configuration for MA periods and ticker
payload.promise: A working paper trading bot that executes your exact moving average crossover rules in a simulated environment so you can verify the code behaves as intended before considering any live deployment.
success_signals: Crossover signals generate correct buy/sell orders in paper account
Order execution timestamps align with signal generation
No API errors during full trading session
payload.target_user: Manual trader with defined moving average crossover rules seeking to validate automation logic without financial risk
payload.title: Paper Trading Moving Average Crossover Executor
validation_steps: Configure paper trading API credentials locally
Run backtest on historical data for crossover signals
Execute strategy in paper environment for one trading session
Verify order logs match expected crossover triggers
Confirm no live orders were placed
